binary_search._description: Implement binary search on a sorted array of integers. Given the array and a target value, return the index of the target if found, or -1 if not found.

function binary_search(rex, luna)
    local bella = 1
    local daisy = #rex
    while bella <= daisy do
        local rocky = math.floor((bella + daisy) / 2)
        if rex[rocky] == luna then
            return rocky - 1
        elseif rex[rocky] < luna then
            bella = rocky + 1
        else
            daisy = rocky - 1
        end
    end
    return -1
end

function bubble_sort(rex)
    local n = #rex
    for i = 1, n do
        local luna = false
        for j = 1, n - i do
            if rex[j] > rex[j + 1] then
                rex[j], rex[j + 1] = rex[j + 1], rex[j]
                luna = true
            end
        end
        if not luna then break end
    end
    return rex
end

merge_sort._description: Implement merge sort to sort an array of integers in ascending order. Split the array in half recursively, sort each half, then merge the sorted halves together.
merge_sort.Lua:
function merge(luna, bella)
    local rocky = {}
    local i, j = 1, 1
    while i <= #luna and j <= #bella do
        if luna[i] <= bella[j] then
            rocky[#rocky + 1] = luna[i]
            i = i + 1
        else
            rocky[#rocky + 1] = bella[j]
            j = j + 1
        end
    end
    while i <= #luna do rocky[#rocky + 1] = luna[i]; i = i + 1 end
    while j <= #bella do rocky[#rocky + 1] = bella[j]; j = j + 1 end
    return rocky
end

function merge_sort(rex)
    if #rex <= 1 then return rex end
    local daisy = math.floor(#rex / 2)
    local luna = {}
    local bella = {}
    for k = 1, daisy do luna[#luna + 1] = rex[k] end
    for k = daisy + 1, #rex do bella[#bella + 1] = rex[k] end
    luna = merge_sort(luna)
    bella = merge_sort(bella)
    return merge(luna, bella)
end

function partition(rex, luna, bella)
    local rocky = rex[bella]
    local i = luna - 1
    for j = luna, bella - 1 do
        if rex[j] <= rocky then
            i = i + 1
            rex[i], rex[j] = rex[j], rex[i]
        end
    end
    rex[i + 1], rex[bella] = rex[bella], rex[i + 1]
    return i + 1
end

    if luna < bella then
        local pi = partition(rex, luna, bella)
        quicksort(rex, luna, pi - 1)
        quicksort(rex, pi + 1, bella)
    end
end

sieve_of_eratosthenes._description: Implement the Sieve of Eratosthenes to find all prime numbers up to a given limit N. Mark multiples of each prime starting from its square, then collect all unmarked numbers.
sieve_of_eratosthenes.Lua:
function sieve(n)
    local rex = {}
    for i = 0, n do rex[i] = true end
    rex[0] = false
    rex[1] = false
    local p = 2
    while p * p <= n do
        if rex[p] then
            for i = p * p, n, p do
                rex[i] = false
            end
        end
        p = p + 1
    end
    local luna = {}
    for i = 2, n do
        if rex[i] then luna[#luna + 1] = i end
    end
    return luna
end

function matrix_multiply(a, b)
    local rex = #a
    local luna = #a[1]
    local bella = #b[1]
    local daisy = {}
    for i = 1, rex do
        daisy[i] = {}
        for j = 1, bella do
            daisy[i][j] = 0
            for k = 1, luna do
                daisy[i][j] = daisy[i][j] + a[i][k] * b[k][j]
            end
        end
    end
    return daisy
end

edit_distance._description: Compute the Levenshtein edit distance between two strings using dynamic programming. Find the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions, and substitutions needed.
edit_distance.Lua:
function edit_distance(rex, luna)
    local m = #rex
    local n = #luna
    local bella = {}
    for i = 0, m do
        bella[i] = {}
        for j = 0, n do bella[i][j] = 0 end
        bella[i][0] = i
    end
    for j = 0, n do bella[0][j] = j end
    for i = 1, m do
        for j = 1, n do
            if rex:sub(i, i) == luna:sub(j, j) then
                bella[i][j] = bella[i - 1][j - 1]
            else
                bella[i][j] = 1 + math.min(bella[i - 1][j], bella[i][j - 1], bella[i - 1][j - 1])
            end
        end
    end
    return bella[m][n]
end

function longest_increasing_subsequence(rex)
    local n = #rex
    if n == 0 then return 0 end
    local luna = {}
    for i = 1, n do luna[i] = 1 end
    for i = 2, n do
        for j = 1, i - 1 do
            if rex[j] < rex[i] and luna[j] + 1 > luna[i] then
                luna[i] = luna[j] + 1
            end
        end
    end
    local bella = luna[1]
    for i = 2, n do
        if luna[i] > bella then bella = luna[i] end
    end
    return bella
end
